title: Why do some people believe the moon landings were a hoax?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant examine why some people believe the 1969 Apollo moon landings were a hoax. They cover the Cold War and space race motives behind the theory, NASA's 1960s goal set by Kennedy, and the 0.014 percent failure-odds claim attributed to Bill Casing of Rocketdyne. They walk through the main visual "evidence": the letter C rock, the varying shadow lengths, the waving American flag (explained by a horizontal wire), and dust behavior in a vacuum. They also discuss Ralph Renee's claim about secret grain aid to the Soviet Union, NASA funding and the Vietnam War distraction theory, and modern lunar orbiters (India's Chandrayaan, Japan's Kaguya, US Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter) that could photograph the landing sites. The episode ends with listener mail from Ben in Ontario about a bicycle accident he attributes to possession by the Egyptian god Horus, which is unrelated to the moon topic. Sponsor reads appear at the start.
topics: Ralph Renee grain aid Soviet Union

segments.title: Sponsor reads and opening
segments.summary: Camry and GoDaddy sponsor reads, then the hosts introduce the moon landing hoax topic.

segments.title: Opening banter and the Rocketdyne odds claim
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the idea that people doubt the 1969 landing. They cite Bill Casing's claim that the odds of landing and returning a man were 0.014 percent, which proved wrong. They agree to discuss the topic without a conspiratorial tone.

segments.title: Cold War motives and Kennedy's moon goal
segments.summary: The theory holds that the moon landing was staged to embarrass the Soviet Union in the space race. The hosts note Kennedy's 1960 goal to reach the moon by 1969 and the technology of the time.

segments.title: The C rock and the shadow lengths
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a moon rock that appears to bear the letter C, which NASA attributes to a hair or scratch on the lens, and varying shadow lengths in photos. Josh argues the shadow differences are natural on uneven terrain and that NASA would not have released flawed footage if faking it.

segments.title: Waving flag, lunar dust, and vacuum sound stage
segments.summary: The flag appears to move, which NASA explains with a horizontal wire across its top. Dust kicked up by walking and the rover falls back quickly in the thin atmosphere, which the hosts argue would be hard to fake in a vacuum sound stage.

segments.title: Ralph Renee and the secret grain aid
segments.summary: Ralph Renee argued that the US quietly sent large amounts of grain aid to the Soviet Union right after the landing, which the hosts consider a tenuous argument against a hoax.

segments.title: NASA funding, Vietnam distraction, and modern orbiters
segments.summary: The hosts discuss NASA's roughly fifty billion dollars in funding and the theory that the moon program distracted from the Vietnam War, noting NASA funding dropped after the last landing. They point out that modern orbiters from India, Japan, and the US have cameras that may not have enough resolution to photograph the landing sites.

segments.title: Listener mail: Ben's possession story
segments.summary: Ben from Ontario shares a story about a bicycle accident and amnesia, which he attributes to possession by the Egyptian god Horus. He cites marks on his eye that resemble Horus paintings. The hosts thank him and invite more listener stories.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and invite email at stuffpodcast@howstuffworks.com. Sponsor line closes the episode.
